note: Briefs for the new unified-app features (ADR-0009). Source of the Spec Kit prompts rendered into Auto-Creator.md section 20 and of the UA gates in the migration ledger. Paths marked (new) do not exist yet; names of new types are proposals to be confirmed against real code during /speckit-plan.

constitution_amendment.prompt: /speckit-constitution Amend the VisualCore constitution from 1.5.0 to 2.0.0 (MAJOR: scope and Principle V are redefined) to adopt ADR-0009. Keep Principles I, II, II-a, III, IV, VI, VII, VIII, IX and X and every app-scoped rule for A01-A04 in force; change only what ADR-0009 changes, and record a dated rationale that cites ADR-0009. Required amendments: (1) Scope: one iPhone/iPad application, VisualCore, with one shippable app target and modular registered experiences; the Showcase and the harnesses stay non-shipping; the 25 original apps and all round games are experiences, not separate apps. (2) Add Principle XI, One App and Stable Experience Identity: exactly one shippable app target and bundle identifier; every experience has an immutable id '<code>.<slug>' from docs/catalog/experience-catalog.json; experiences never depend on each other; ProjectM types stay out of the app. (3) Add Principle XII, One Purchase and No Advertising (NON-NEGOTIABLE): free download; exactly one non-consumable StoreKit 2 product at USD 1.99 unlocking every premium experience including future ones; no ads, ad SDKs, ad identifiers, rewarded ads, subscriptions, consumables, external payment paths, dark patterns or required accounts; premium gating at routing and at experience activation; the test-only entitlement fixture must be absent from shipping Release binaries. (4) Add Principle XIII, Code-Driven Visuals: all worlds and signature effects are GLSL, procedural meshes, SDFs, particles and deterministic animation on the existing OpenGL ES to ANGLE to Metal path; no required human-made models, purchased art packs, prompt-generated images or external image services. (5) Redefine Principle V, Implementation Before Devices: all 100 launch experiences (50 free, 50 premium) are implemented and pass host and simulator acceptance, and ImplementationLock-100 is recorded by scripts/migration_ledger.py, before any physical-device install, launch or test of the unified app; then D1, D2, D3 in that order, 100 experiences each; D3 stays on iPadOS 26.5; historical device observations never certify the unified build. (6) Principle VIII: one PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy for the app, audited against the built product. (7) Development Workflow: feature numbering and ID namespaces of Auto-Creator.md section 19; the legacy ledger .autonomy/state.json keeps the A-phase gates; .autonomy/migration/ledger.json holds every new gate; commits stay on the migration branch and are never pushed to main until the owner merges. (8) App-Scoped Rules: keep the A01-A04 rules, reworded from 'app' to 'experience' only where the directory or target wording would otherwise be false. (9) Governance precedence: Apple and toolchain behavior and observed tests, then Auto-Creator.md and CLAUDE.md, then this constitution and ADRs, then the planning archive, then generated code. Do not delete or weaken any requirement that ADR-0009 does not supersede. After amending, update the Sync Impact Report, run python3 scripts/validate_docs.py, and write ADR-0010 recording the amendment.

features.title: ExperienceKit: the experience contract
absorbs: R02-F23 puzzle contract (the lifecycle and digest parts; solver certification stays in R02-F23)
features.scope: Define the contract every experience implements, adapting existing VisualCore surfaces instead of duplicating them: lifecycle (prepare(seed:), activate, suspend, resume, deactivate), fixed-step update, draw through RenderScene, normalized input with typed accept or reject, snapshot, restore, reset, diagnostics and automation hooks. Pure parts (state machine, snapshot envelope, digests, conformance helpers) go in VisualCoreExperience; the SwiftUI and RenderHost parts go in a new module VisualCoreExperienceHost in Packages/VisualCoreRendering.
acceptance: The lifecycle is a pure reducer (registered, preparing, ready, active, suspended, deactivating, inactive, failed) with exhaustive transition tests; illegal transitions are rejected and counted
prepare(seed:) is deterministic: the same seed gives the same initial state digest; a reusable ExperienceConformance test helper checks this for any experience
restore(snapshot()) reproduces the digest; reset() equals a fresh prepare with the same seed; snapshots are versioned envelopes with migrations
Input is normalized into domain actions; a rejected action leaves the digest unchanged and returns a typed reason
Update runs in fixed steps independent of frame rate; drawing reads immutable state; no GPU result decides an outcome
Diagnostics expose state, seed, step index, quality tier, live GPU resource counts, last error and digest
Automation hooks compile only under DEBUG or VISUALCORE_AUTOMATION
A sample experience used only by tests exercises the whole contract on the host and on both simulator runtimes; public API documented and baselined
evidence: python3 scripts/xcodebuild_package.py --package Packages/VisualCoreRendering --scheme VisualCoreRendering-Package --destination sim-27.2 --action test --result-name ua-f02-ios27
python3 scripts/xcodebuild_package.py --package Packages/VisualCoreRendering --scheme VisualCoreRendering-Package --destination sim-26.5 --action test --result-name ua-f02-ios26

features.title: Experience host and session lifecycle

features.scope: Implement ExperienceSession and ExperienceHostView in VisualCoreExperienceHost: one active experience at a time, RenderHost creation through the session with a resource budget, activation and deactivation with proof of zero live GPU resources, failure isolation, cancellation, scene-phase handling, memory-pressure handling and context-loss recovery.
acceptance: Only one session is active; opening another deactivates the first before the new one prepares
After deactivation the session's ResourceRegistry reports zero live resources and zero leaked; 50 open and close cycles of the sample experience keep these at zero on both simulator runtimes
An error in prepare, setup or render shows a failure view with Retry and Back; the app stays usable and the failure is recorded in diagnostics
Leaving during prepare cancels the work; no callback arrives after deactivation
Background suspends (clock stopped, host paused) and foreground resumes without catching up; interruptions are honored
A memory warning sheds caches; if the session is still over its budget it deactivates with a message
A forced context recreation rebuilds GPU objects from CPU state and keeps the state digest
Experience and app sources contain no direct GL or EGL calls (scripts/check_app_isolation.py extended to experience modules)

features.title: Session state, per-experience persistence, reset and restore

features.scope: Give each experience an isolated storage namespace and the app a restorable session: storage root Application Support/Experiences/<id>/ and defaults prefix exp.<id>., autosave at suspend and safe points, restore after relaunch, per-experience and global reset, versioned migrations and a container inventory test.
acceptance: An experience can only reach its own storage through its context; a test proves two experiences cannot read each other's data

Reset experience clears exactly that namespace; Reset all data clears every namespace and the session state
Each experience with stored data has a migration test from every earlier schema version
A container inventory test lists only allowed files and defaults keys (StoreKit and Metal cache files are allowed after their provenance is checked)
